impl_test_ledger:
[round 1] 45/45 pytest pass on host + lint_fidelity 0 BLOCKING, but differential battery (impl vs pinned vLLM v0.27.1 executed in container, 47 CHECK scenarios) found 2 tests asserting impl-fallback numbers instead of pinned-real behavior — both in the mamba-align config with block_size == hash_block_size:

(1) tests/test_prefix_caching.py::TestHybridFixedPoint::test_num_uncached_common_prefix_tokens — asserts hit==64/boundary==0 then hit==48/boundary==64 for full(16)+mamba(16,'align') hash_bs=16. Pinned real v0.27.1 (differentially executed): hit==0/boundary==64 in BOTH phases. Root cause: real align-mode MambaManager null-pads [NULL x4, single state block] and registers ONLY the last state block (hash[4]@80), unreachable under max_cache_hit_length=num_tokens-1=79, so the mamba group never hits and the fixed point drags the whole lookup to 0 (uncached=64 -> boundary=64); the test's _remove_cached_block_hashes(mamba_blocks[3]) removes a NULL block = no-op on real. Impl's base-class fallback (approved dossier.delete #6) makes the mamba group register all 5 blocks full-attention-like — the asserted numbers are that side effect, not pin behavior.

(2) tests/test_prefix_caching.py::TestMarconiPinning::test_shared_prefix_boundary_written_back — same config/flow, asserts hit==48/boundary==64; real: hit==0/boundary==64. The admission_lookup write-back control flow itself is faithful (anchor-verified vs scheduler.py L744-L766) — only the driving numbers diverge.

Fix (verified on BOTH sides by tester, identical outputs): re-drive both tests in the partial-hit config (full(64)+mamba(64,'align'), hash_bs=16) where the impl substitution is proven byte-exact vs the pin — A(48) -> free -> new_step_starts() -> evict the mamba @48 entry via _remove_cached_block_hashes -> B(80 sharing 48) yields hit==0/boundary==48 (uncached=48) on real and impl alike; annotate the impl-vs-pin boundary for the block_size==hash_block_size config in impl-notes.md. All other 43 tests differentially/anchor verified against the pin (46/47 battery lines byte-identical; implementation code itself faithful, no code changes needed).
